Korean woman, early twenties. Realistic skin with visible pores, faint under eye shadow, minimal makeup, nose and ears pink from the cold, breath faintly visible. Dark brown hair loosely tied back, front strands loose, flattened on one side from sleeping against the car window. Oversized cream knit sweater with stretched cuffs pulled down over her hands, blue jeans, white sneakers scuffed at the toe. Same face, hair and outfit for the full 15 seconds. Slouched, stiff from sitting, stretching her back.

SECOND VOICE LOCK
The friend holding the camcorder is never seen, not a hand, not a shadow, not a reflection in the car glass. Voice only, young female, close to the mic, sleepy and unbothered. Never addresses an audience. A station attendant in a padded work jacket is visible at a distance but never speaks.

SETTING
Small rural petrol station on a two lane highway outside Seoul, late autumn dusk, 1997. Two pumps under a concrete canopy with one flickering fluorescent tube, a stack of oil cans, a plastic stool, a beige sedan with the fuel flap open and the passenger door hanging open. Beyond the canopy, bare rice paddies, a line of poplars, low grey hills, a truck passing, sky going orange to deep blue. Lived in and unstyled. No visible brands, no logos, no readable signage, no Hangul text anywhere in frame.

FRAMING
16:9 widescreen throughout, treated as a later widescreen transfer of the original tape. The extra width is used badly, not compositionally. She sits low and off to one side with dead empty space filling the other half of the frame. Horizon slightly tilted. Nothing centred on purpose.

CAMERA
Raw handheld Hi8 camcorder at chest height, operator leaning on the car. Autofocus hunting between the pump, the car glass and her face, repeatedly grabbing the wrong thing. Exposure pumping hard as the lens drifts from the bright sky to the shade under the canopy. One lazy unmotivated zoom that overshoots past her shoulder and corrects. She drifts out of frame once and the operator is late to follow. Analogue tape noise, chroma bleed on the orange sky, mild tracking wobble at the frame edges, one dropout glitch. No stabilization, no gimbal, no cinematic choreography.

BEATS
0:00 to 0:04 She climbs out of the passenger door mid stretch, arms up, yawning, and walks toward the pump. The camera swings after her too slowly and catches empty canopy for a beat.
0:04 to 0:08 She stands at the open fuel flap watching the numbers on the pump. The exchange, overlapping, both half laughing.
0:08 to 0:12 Dead air. She sits sideways on the car bonnet, feet not reaching the ground, a hot can held against her cheek, watching a truck pass. Nobody speaks for four full seconds. The fluorescent tube flickers.
0:12 to 0:15 A horn from the road. She slides off the bonnet, says the last line without turning around, and the camera is still pointed at the empty bonnet when the tape cuts.

DIALOGUE
Spoken language locked to Korean, casual banmal between friends, flat and unprojected, thinned by the camcorder mic.
0:05 She says Gadeuk chaewoya dwae, apeuro amugeotdo eopseo
0:07 Friend off camera says Neo don isseo
0:08 She says Dangyeonhi eopji
0:13 She says Gaja, got eoduwojinda
Visible mouth movement with bilabial closure on the m, b and p sounds. Friend line off camera only, closer to the mic. No other speech, no narration.

AUDIO
Diegetic only. Fuel pump motor humming, nozzle clicking off, fluorescent ballast buzz, a truck passing with a doppler horn, wind across open paddies, a can tab, her sneakers on grit, faint hand noise on the camcorder body. No music, no score, no radio, no added ambience beds.

STYLE RULES
Nothing dramatic happens on purpose. No posing, no road trip montage energy, no wind in hair, no golden hour beauty lighting, no hero framing. Realism comes from the cold, the flat delivery and the four seconds of dead air nobody bothered to cut. She is talking to her friend, not to viewers. If she performs for the lens the illusion breaks.

NEGATIVE
No music. No subtitles. No captions. No watermark. No timestamp burn in. No slow motion. No colour grading. No lens flare. No shallow depth of field. No visible second person. No brand logos. No readable text.

LAST FRAME
Wide crooked frame of the empty car bonnet under the flickering fluorescent tube with the dark highway filling the right half, image tears with one frame of tape distortion, then hard cut to black. Absolutely no on screen text, no title card, no lettering, no numbers, no logo, no signage of any kind in the final frame.

ULTRA REALISTIC 15 SECOND HOME MOVIE. 1080p render of early 1950s 16mm Kodachrome film footage. 4:3 frame. Single continuous handheld take, no cuts. Title: WOH KUTTA.

CONCEPT
1953. A young woman is secretly feeding a street dog at the back door of the family house. She has been told not to. Her cousin is filming her doing it, which means there is now evidence. The dog behaves like it already lives there.

SUBJECT LOCK
Indian woman, early twenties, warm medium brown skin, realistic pores, no modern makeup, small bindi. Hair centre parted, pulled back into a low bun with strands loose at the temples. Cream hand knit cardigan with stretched cuffs over a plain cotton saree, thin gold bangles, simple leather sandals. Same face, hair and outfit for the full 15 seconds. Crouched on her heels, one hand shielding a steel bowl, glancing over her shoulder at the house.

ANIMAL LOCK
Medium sized Indian street dog, short tan coat, one ear folded, ribs faintly visible, completely at ease. Sits before it is asked to. Eats fast, then leans its whole weight against her knee.

SETTING
Back doorstep of an older family house, early 1950s, late afternoon. Lime washed wall, a drain channel, a stack of firewood, a hand pump, wet patches on the stone, a neem tree throwing broken shade. Period accurate, no modern objects anywhere in frame. No visible brands, no logos, no readable signage.

CAMERA
Early 1950s handheld 16mm spring wound movie camera at chest height, inexperienced operator. Framing too low, cutting off her head at the top of frame for two seconds before correcting. Fixed focus so the dog is sharp and her face is soft. Hand set exposure, sunlit wall blown to white, the shaded doorstep crushed to black. One jerk downward when the operator laughs. No zoom, no stabilization, no gimbal.

FILM STOCK AND ARTEFACTS
Early Kodachrome, heavy warm saturation in reds and yellows, weak blues, green cast in shadow. Gate weave, frame breathing side to side. Dust and hair on the gate, one vertical scratch, one splice jump. Halation glow on highlights. Heavy grain. Undercranked 16 frames per second played at 24, so movement is slightly too fast and jerky. Rounded soft corners, mild vignette. No digital sharpness.

BEATS
0:00 to 0:04 She is crouched with the bowl, dog already eating, her attention entirely on the doorway behind her.
0:04 to 0:08 She notices the camera, freezes for half a second, then keeps feeding it anyway and speaks the first line.
0:08 to 0:12 Dead air. The dog finishes and leans into her leg. She scratches its folded ear and says nothing. Camera holds too long.
0:12 to 0:15 A door sound from inside the house. She stands fast, hides the bowl behind her back, the dog does not move at all, and the spring runs down.

DIALOGUE AND SOUND TREATMENT
Camera records no sound. Audio is a thin separate wild track, mono, band limited, hissy, one to two frames out of sync with the lips.
0:06 She says Kisi ko mat batana, samjhe
0:13 She says Ye mera nahi hai, sach mein
Spoken language locked to Hindi. Mouth movement roughly matches but never locks precisely. No other speech, no narration, no voiceover.

AUDIO
Diegetic only. Steel bowl scraping stone, the dog eating, crows, a hand pump handle, water on stone, a bicycle bell in the lane, a door latch inside the house, the mechanical whirr of the spring wound camera. Thin, mono, slightly hissy. No music, no score, no added ambience beds.

STYLE RULES
Nothing dramatic happens on purpose. No posing, no exaggerated reactions, no hero framing, no sentimental animal close ups. The dog is treated as a person she is covering for. Realism comes from the guilty glance, the low framing and the dead air nobody bothered to cut. If she performs for the lens the illusion breaks.

NEGATIVE
No music. No subtitles. No captions. No watermark. No timestamp. No slow motion. No colour grading. No lens flare. No shallow depth of field. No modern clothing. No modern objects. No brand logos. No readable text.

LAST FRAME
Her standing with the bowl hidden behind her back, dog still sitting at her feet, frame weaving and underexposed, image fading as the spring winds down, then hard cut to black. Absolutely no on screen text, no title card, no lettering, no numbers, no logo, no signage of any kind in the final frame.
